verdict: The trust head DOES respond to degradation: perturbing one camera moves its own score while the untouched five stay put, separating by 0.1652 on average. On clean frames it sits at 0.584 +/- 0.0002 across all cameras, which is the correct behaviour for a head trained to detect injected faults -- it is a fault detector, not a scene-quality score, and should be read that way.
caveats: stat_calibrated is False in this checkpoint, so the head's statistics branch runs on default buffers and the fused score leans on its CNN branch. calibrate_trust_stats.py exists to fill those in and has not been run against this checkpoint.
Perturbations are applied to the model's 90x160 input tensor, not to full-resolution images.
24 keyframes, one camera faulted at a time.
gradio_app.py hard-codes clean trust at 0.795; the live head returns 0.584 on clean nuScenes frames. That constant is stale and should be read from the model.
